title: Jitterbug Flip3 or Smart5: Simple Phones and What the Lively Plan Really Costs
subtitle: A plain-English look at two easy-to-use Jitterbug phones from Lively, and the monthly fees that come with them.
excerpt: The Jitterbug Flip3 and Smart5 are built for easy calling, but the price on the phone is only part of the story. Here is what each offers and how to figure a year of service, based on Lively's own pages.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Many of us do not want a phone that does a hundred things. We want one that shows big numbers and makes it easy to call the people we love. Tiny icons and endless menus can turn a simple call into a frustrating chore.

Lively, the company behind the Jitterbug name, sells two phones aimed at that need: the Jitterbug Flip3, a flip phone with big buttons, and the Jitterbug Smart5, a smartphone with a simplified menu. Both need a Lively service plan, so it pays to look at the monthly bill, not just the price of the phone. One note: this article draws only on Lively's own pages. We did not compare other brands or read independent reviews, and other makers do sell simple phones too.

The Flip3 is for people who mainly want to call and text. It folds shut, has physical buttons you can feel, and a 3.2-inch screen with large text. Lively describes the keypad as having "Big, backlit, tactile buttons," meaning the keys are lit from behind and easy to feel with your fingers.

The Smart5 is a full smartphone (a phone that can run apps and browse the internet) with a much larger 6.75-inch screen. Instead of rows of icons, it uses a simple list-based menu. It also offers voice typing, so you can speak a text message instead of typing it.

Both phones list Wi-Fi calling, which lets you make calls over your home internet when cell signal is weak. Both pages also list hearing aid compatibility ratings, as Lively states them. These numbers do not replace a hearing test or a hearing aid fitting, so ask your audiologist or doctor how a phone will work with your own hearing aids.

Lively advertises Flip3 plans "as low as $14.99/mo." and Smart5 Unlimited Talk & Text plans as low as $19.99 a month (November 2026), with no long-term contracts or cancellation fees. The pages say these prices require the basic plan with paperless billing. Check which plan you actually need and what it costs before relying on the lowest figure.

On top of that, there is a $3.23 monthly admin fee, plus taxes and surcharges that vary by location. The Flip3 page also lists a $35 one-time activation fee. For the Flip3, $14.99 plus $3.23 a month, times 12, is about $219 a year before taxes and surcharges, plus the activation fee and the phone. That is our own arithmetic from the page figures, assuming the basic plan applies to you.

For the Smart5, $19.99 plus $3.23 a month, times 12, is about $279 a year before taxes and surcharges. That is also an estimate from the page figures. The Smart5 page does not list an activation fee in the information we have, so ask Lively whether one applies.

items: Monthly fees: add the admin fee, taxes and surcharges to the advertised plan price to see the real bill.
Emergency help: the Help button reaches 24/7 help only with Lively's paid Urgent Response upgrade. Ask what it costs before you count on it.
Buttons and screen: if fingers or eyesight make touch screens hard, a flip phone with physical keys may be easier.
Battery: Lively lists up to 12 hours of talk time for the Flip3, and any battery holds less charge as it ages.
Number transfer: if you want to keep your current number, ask Lively about moving it over before you buy.
Returns: check the return policy and how long you have to decide.

sections.content: Setting it up and using it well

If an adult child is helping, consider setting up the phone together. Charge it fully first, then add the most important contacts so they are a button press away. On the Smart5, practice opening the list menu and using voice typing a few times until it feels natural.

Families may want to look at the Lively Link app, which Lively says sends an alert to a relative's smartphone if the phone's user contacts Urgent Response. Urgent Response is a paid upgrade, and costs for Lively Link or other care services may apply, so ask Lively for current prices first.

These are phones, not medical alert systems. They do not detect falls, and the Help button only reaches 24/7 help with a paid upgrade. The Smart5, like any smartphone, can still receive scam calls and texts, so a simple menu is not a shield against fraud. In an emergency, call 911.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: A good simple phone is the one that gets used. If calling and texting are all you need, the Flip3 keeps things clear and costs less per month. If you want a bigger screen and a full smartphone, the Smart5 offers more, at a higher monthly price. Sale prices and plan prices can change, so check current prices and add up the full yearly cost before you decide.
